plan: To prioritize capital preservation, we will exit all leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL, MUU, METU, PLTU, MSFU) to reduce risk.
QQQI will be trimmed to 20% to cure the concentration breach and align with the conservative single-name limit.
This approach aims for a stable portfolio with minimal drawdown.
A significant cash buffer will be maintained for stability.
conservative.read: This conservative plan targets a modest ~1.5%/month return, focusing on capital preservation. It significantly reduces portfolio volatility by eliminating leveraged positions. Expect lower drawdowns, but also more limited upside potential.

plan: QQQI will be trimmed to 25% to address the concentration breach and maintain balance.
Leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL, MUU, METU, PLTU, MSFU) will be trimmed to small allocations to reduce overall leverage.
This strategy blends broad index exposure with quality tech, aiming for risk-first growth.
A cash buffer of approximately 10% will be maintained.
balanced.read: The balanced plan aims for ~2.5%/month growth by managing risk and reducing leverage. It seeks a middle ground between capital preservation and aggressive growth. Expect moderate volatility and potential drawdowns.

plan: QQQI will be trimmed to 20% to cure the concentration breach, freeing capital for higher-growth opportunities.
Leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL, MUU, METU, PLTU, MSFU) will be increased to lean into growth.
This strategy concentrates in higher-scoring setups, using leverage to amplify returns.
A smaller cash buffer will be maintained, accepting higher risk for potential growth.
aggressive.read: This aggressive plan targets ~4%/month growth by leveraging high-beta assets. It significantly increases both upside potential and drawdown risk. Be aware of daily decay in leveraged ETFs and the potential for rapid losses if stops are not strictly adhered to.

plan: All leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL, MUU, METU, PLTU, MSFU) will be sold to reduce volatility and focus on income.
QQQI will be increased to 30% to enhance monthly distributions and align with income goals.
This plan prioritizes steady income and low drawdown over growth.

income.read: The income plan targets ~1%/month, prioritizing steady distributions and capital preservation. It significantly reduces exposure to high-beta assets. While aiming for reliable income, remember distributions are variable and NAV can still decline in market downturns.
